dedupe_keys.name: usgs pfdf python library for postfire debris flow hazard assessment of stream networks

description: pfdf is a USGS Python library, published on code.usgs.gov with documentation on USGS code pages, that supports postfire debris-flow hazard assessments and research. Contents: routines to download assessment datasets, analyse watersheds, delineate and filter stream segment networks, compute earth-system variables for each segment, estimate debris-flow likelihood with the models of Staley and others (2017), estimate potential sediment volumes with the models of Gartner and others (2014), classify relative hazard with the methods of Cannon and others (2010), and export results to Shapefile and GeoJSON. Producer: USGS; the code sits in the Geologic Hazards Science Center group on code.usgs.gov (ghsc/lhp). Coverage: burned areas, with the source models calibrated in the western United States. Format and access: open source Python (3.11 to 3.13) with tutorials, a user guide and a full API reference; releases carry DOIs listed on the citation page. Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (repository licence). Caveats: the underlying empirical models were developed from western US data, which limits their transfer elsewhere; the library prepares hazard estimates, not impacts on assets. Simulation uses: hazard layers for exposure of roads, culverts, bridges and water supply intakes below burn scars, and emergency response planning after wildfires. Related records: data-usfs-wildfire-hazard-potential and data-caltrans-wildfire-vulnerability-2020.
